advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert peer subprocess liveness (returncode==0 and/or an asserted PRESENCE log line from the same stdout) before trusting `not _drake_reconverge_warned_at_pre_lock_site(peer_sync.stdout)`.
evidence: `peer_sync = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", _DRAKE_SYNC_CODE], ... check=False, timeout=30)` — run with check=False, returncode never asserted
`assert not _drake_reconverge_warned_at_pre_lock_site(peer_sync.stdout)` (line 987) — absence-only oracle on child stdout with no producer-liveness anchor
Helper swallows malformed output: `except json.JSONDecodeError: continue` then returns False, so a crash traceback on stdout counts as 'not warned'
ABSENCE rationale: a peer subprocess that dies before the warning site leaves the tracker unmutated and emits no matching WARNING, satisfying AC1 vacuously — same result as the fix working
advisory.finding: Integration test AC1's core assertion `assert not _drake_reconverge_warned_at_pre_lock_site(peer_sync.stdout)` is a fail-open oracle: it trusts the ABSENCE of the pre-lock warning from a child subprocess's stdout with no liveness check on that subprocess. `peer_sync` is run with check=False and neither its returncode, nor non-empty stdout, nor any PRESENCE from the capture is asserted before the absence is trusted; the helper additionally swallows JSONDecodeError and returns False. A peer that crashed on import, raised before reaching the warning site, or emitted an unexpected format therefore also yields 'not warned' — the passing verdict — so the check cannot distinguish the fixed behavior from its own producer failing to run. The subsequent tracker-state asserts anchor the tracker, not the peer subprocess.
scenarios: Peer reconverge subprocess raises during import or before the pre-lock site regresses
A future change alters the JSON log shape so the WARNING line no longer decodes
advisory.suggested_fix: Before the absence assertion, add `assert peer_sync.returncode == 0, peer_sync.stderr` and assert a PRESENCE marker (e.g. a reconverge start/skip DEBUG line) is present in peer_sync.stdout, so the 'not warned' verdict is only trusted when the producer demonstrably ran to the classification site.
